urn:eigenius:core:description: The kinase-activity-remaining function with Hill coefficient n=1: `h(c) = ic50 / (ic50 + c)`. Free variables `c` (compound concentration) and `ic50` (the IC50 parameter). Foundation for the kinase-grounded Symbolics demos: substitution to specialise on a measured IC50, differentiation to get the slope at a concentration, equation-form to relate to the inhibition curve.
The Hill function specialised at IC50 = 42 nM (EIG_0042 vs CDK2 from R0001). Free variable: `c` only.
Substituting `ic50 := 42.0` in the Hill function yields the EIG_0042-CDK2-specific form. AutoOnLoad re-runs `Symbolics.substitute` and confirms.

The derivative `dh/dc` of the Hill function: `-ic50 / (ic50 + c)^2`. Used downstream by IntervalArithmetic to bound the slope of the inhibition curve on a concentration domain (the natural Phase-19f handoff once 19d/19f Comorphisms are wired).
Claims that the derivative of the Hill function with respect to `c` is `-ic50 / (ic50 + c)^2`. AutoOnLoad re-runs `Symbolics.derivative` + `simplify` and compares. Holds modulo simplification.
